content: The Codex quota footer uses ModelRegistry.getApiKeyForProvider plus readStoredCredential because Pi 0.80.8 removed extension access to ModelRegistry.authStorage.
pi-tools extension settings will support manually edited global and trusted project config files plus an in-Pi management command/UI.
The `/pi-tools` configuration UI should render every setting registered by pi-tools extensions from the initial implementation.
Remove the legacy `/codex-quota` shortcut; footer quota settings are managed exclusively through the unified `/pi-tools` interface and shared config.
Pi loads each extension with an isolated module cache, so settings definitions are synchronized to the `/pi-tools` manager through Pi's shared event bus rather than a shared module-level registry.
`/pi-tools` persists each edit immediately but defers extension reload until the settings UI closes, allowing batch edits without reopening the UI.
Tool-output compression defaults to observe; any profile must be explicitly set to apply before it can store raw output and replace a result.
Tool-output compression will use a single private SQLite store with WAL, `synchronous=FULL`, and serialized write-safe multi-instance transactions rather than separate artifact files and an index.

Compression will start as a result-side exact-duplicate-reuse foundation without permanently excluding future techniques; apply behavior is configured by tool scope rather than per-result user approval, and retrieval is an agent tool rather than a user workflow.
Stored tool-output references are retrievable only by the session that created them, and retrieval is limited to UTF-8-safe chunks no larger than 48 KiB.

Apply mode stores the first eligible text result unchanged and replaces only a later same-session byte-identical result when its committed retrieval reference saves at least 16 bytes; all uncertainty fails open.
Future compression work will use aggregate usage data and agent assistance to propose trusted-project output profiles, but every profile requires explicit human review and enablement.

The Go test profile defaults to observe via `profiles.test.go.mode`, aggregates successful normal or verbose package summaries with verbose passing detail raw-only after durable storage, and leaves failed, malformed, composite, or never-worse results unchanged.

Tool-output compression uses a generic profile registry with category-aligned profiles.<category>.<profile>.mode settings and no compatibility aliases or migrations for unreleased profile architecture.
Implement the safe generic bash JSON/JSONL profile despite modest local corpus savings because other workflows may emit substantially more structured output.
The code-search product is scoped to token-efficient code navigation and retrieval; impact analysis, quality intelligence, and Git analytics belong to separate extensions.

Code-search discovery and orientation results will offer user-selectable structured or directly readable compact response styles through shared pi-tools settings, without a MUNCH-like encoded wire format.
The code-search extension will expose four focused composable tools—code_search, code_outline, code_get, and code_context—rather than an action-routed umbrella tool.
Code search will never return raw source; only code_get and code_context deliver bounded source, and any exact-one-result shortcut requires later evidence before consideration.
Code search is limited to the current Pi project root, supports configurable root-relative ignored paths such as docs/**, and will not search external roots or other worktrees.
Code search must honor .gitignore and configurable additive root-relative ignores; excluded files are neither indexed nor retrievable and exclusions are disclosed in result coverage.
Code search will use a persistent project-local index under .pi/ that is excluded from Git; source retention and refresh policy remain separate decisions.
The .pi code-search index stores metadata only, never copied source bodies; code retrieval validates current files, reparses changed files, and reads exact live byte spans.
Code search schedules a non-blocking worker-thread job at Pi session start to check for and create the project-local index when absent.
Code search validates and incrementally reparses on tool use; its session-scoped filesystem watcher is an opt-in acceleration configured through global or trusted-project settings.
Code search will use Tree-sitter as its primary parsing foundation through a capability registry, with language-specific fallbacks only where needed.
Pi-tools will install all grammars it promises with the main package, lazily load them when encountered, and never require per-language activation or runtime grammar downloads.
Code search will begin with a small curated set of AST-supported languages rather than promising jCodeMunch-scale broad coverage.
Code search provides full AST support for TypeScript/JavaScript variants, Python, and Go; other eligible files use explicit text-search fallback until added through tested releases.
Code search will not include semantic or embedding-based search.
Code search includes filtered AST symbol and literal text search, identifier-aware lexical ranking, and explicit fuzzy matching, while excluding semantic search.

Code context returns selected source plus deduplicated imports and containing-declaration headers by default; neighbours, imported definitions, and tests are explicit opt-ins under one target-first budget.

Code-search discovery uses selectable structured labelled blocks or compact stable rows with mandatory identity/safety fields, while source is verbatim and every result/budget truncation is explicit under token and byte ceilings.

Code-search results report fresh/refreshing/partial/degraded coverage, make zero-result claims only within eligible indexed files, use live validated source, skip symlinks and unsafe files, never execute code, and never transmit code or metadata.
Code search defaults to observe but is completely dormant in untrusted directories; only trusted projects may create .pi state, index, observe local metrics, or expose code tools in apply mode.

Code-search metrics are extension-wide global daily aggregates with 90-day default retention, recording observe baselines and apply-mode delivery estimates without source, query, path, network transmission, or counterfactual savings claims.
Code search will use native Node Tree-sitter bindings and native grammars for its supported languages, without a WASM fallback unless validation reveals unavoidable host incompatibility.

Code search ships a pinned official native Tree-sitter stack with compiler-free support for macOS arm64/x64, Linux x64, and Windows x64; Linux/Windows arm64 are initially unsupported and no peer bypass or custom grammar binaries are used.
Code search will retain the direct zero-dependency ignore package rather than owning or vendoring a custom .gitignore matcher.
Code-search uses a TypeScript worker launched with Node type stripping after validation through a Pi-style production installation; no CommonJS worker bootstrap is retained.

Explicit code_search text fallback may transiently invoke local rg over worker-approved eligible files and return only match metadata; neither source text nor rg output may be persisted or returned, and fuzzy matching remains symbol-only.
Task subagents are explicitly activated, session-scoped interactive workers; users continue conversing with the main Pi agent, which remains the sole orchestration and control point.
Subagent visibility should be available through the main Pi interaction while work runs, with the main agent remaining the user's only control surface rather than a second worker chat.

Event-driven worker milestones, completion, failure, and blocker reports that automatically wake the main agent are an option under consideration alongside call-and-response coordination, not a settled product decision.

Task workers must have broad routine work capability to fulfill delegated tasks; human control should govern goals, scope, and consequential actions rather than require confirmation for ordinary investigation, edits, and verification.
Task-worker activation must not require or judge a Git branch; it reports the current branch and starting commit when available while workflow responsibility remains with the user.

Task workers use a hybrid coordination model: they run independently with detailed task records and UI activity, while the main agent receives only compact run-complete, blocked, or needs-decision handoffs and directs subsequent runs.

Main-agent detail retrieval is report-first, then a focused question to the same persistent worker session; the worker retains execution context and returns another bounded response, while direct artifact inspection is a fallback.

Each active workstream uses a worker-maintained human-readable plain-text running log with terse appended updates and a compact recovery metadata header; it supports compaction and main/worker reconstruction after restart, while location/restart behavior remain open.
After Pi restart, interrupted worker workstreams are restored as paused from their durable state; the main agent decides whether to resume an existing worker session or recreate one.
For task workers, explicit Stop pauses and preserves the workstream for later resume, while separate explicit Cancel terminally ends it.

While Pi remains open, paused task workers retain their live session/process and detailed context; the durable journal is for recovery after cancellation, failure, or Pi shutdown rather than ordinary resume.
Paused task workstreams have no automatic timeout or eviction and remain available until explicitly resumed/cancelled or the parent Pi session ends.
Research jobs are explicitly requested then mostly fire-and-forget; on completion the main agent automatically processes and presents a concise cited result even while other work is being discussed.
Research jobs retain their source material and intermediate artifacts for later inspection while the main agent receives only a concise cited synthesis by default.
When research is explicitly linked to an active task workstream, the main agent automatically provides that worker with the relevant cited synthesis and never the raw source material.
Worker/job visibility defaults to one compact status line showing identity, phase, elapsed time, and last meaningful action, with the detailed activity timeline collapsed until inspected.
Expanded worker timelines show chronological tool calls, worker-to-main reports, and main-to-worker instructions, with raw large outputs collapsed behind their corresponding entries.
Worker UI is inspection-only; pause, stop, redirect, checkpoint-summary, and detail-retrieval actions are requested through normal conversation with the main agent.
A parent Pi session may retain multiple simultaneous task workers; their coordination handoffs remain bounded and routed through the main agent.

The subagent product excludes consequential external operations—remote Git, deployment, infrastructure/production data, spending, publishing, and communication—and targets local/repository work plus research.
Subagents have a persistent enabled/disabled setting integrated with the existing pi-tools configuration system.
Initial subagent configuration has one combined maximum-concurrent-workers setting covering both task workers and research jobs; separate caps are deferred.
Subagent model selection is included in the initial persistent settings surface to support users who use models different from the main agent, even though the current user expects to use one model.
Initial subagent model configuration has two defaults—one for task workers and one for research jobs—with each able to inherit the main agent's current model.
Subagent retention and display behavior are deferred from the initial settings surface to keep it limited to enabled state, combined concurrency, and task/research model defaults.

Initial subagent settings are enabled state, one combined concurrency cap, and task-worker/research-job model defaults that may inherit the main model; task objective, context, linkage, and operational instructions remain per-workstream.
The combined subagent concurrency cap defaults to 2, while the main agent delegates only explicit independently valuable work rather than filling available capacity.
Persistent pi-tools workstreams will use separate in-process SDK AgentSession instances rather than RPC subprocesses, with context isolation but no implied OS sandbox.

Initial subagent workers use Pi’s normal trusted-project capabilities and an instruction-level stop-and-report rule for consequential external actions, with no sandbox or restrictive bespoke tool runtime.
Subagent manifests, journals, reports, recovery records, and persisted SDK sessions are uncommitted local artifacts under tmp/subagents/ rather than repository source state.

Subagents should use proactive delegation: during ordinary conversation the main agent independently launches bounded parallelizable research or task work without a user launch request, while retaining intent, consequential decisions, and acceptance.

The Subagent workstreams widget should be a live-status surface rather than history: hide it when no workstream needs attention, omit settled work, and show only concise current state plus the latest meaningful activity for active or attention-needed workers.
memory_remember must show canonical stored content only in its TUI renderer while keeping concise raw tool-result agent context and hidden project-memory injection unchanged.

The /pi-tools UI will be a two-level navigator with write scope and extension entries at root, extension-specific settings on detail screens, Esc returning to root, and unchanged command-line setting semantics.

Codex weekly quota color uses a capped 14-percentage-point-per-day remaining target: green at/above target, yellow at/above half target, red below half, with fixed bands only when reset time is unavailable.
Subagent delegation policy must apply to bounded implementation work regardless of whether it originated from a planning ticket, user request, bug report, or ad-hoc task.
Subagent guidance must explicitly name preserving main-agent context by isolating detailed investigation, tool output, implementation churn, and test-debug loops behind bounded handoffs.
Subagent delegation improvements will remain advisory; a hard tool-call gate requiring worker launch before parent edits/writes is rejected as too complex.

Subagent guidance will advise delegation for every repository implementation change regardless of origin; main-agent direct work is limited to answering, planning, and non-repository actions, without a hard enforcement gate.

Worker completions use a persisted inbox with no separate badge; the workstreams widget shows only agent, title/purpose, and status including pending-inbox states, without last-action text or automatic user interruption.

Deferred worker handoffs must be available to a main agent that intentionally waits for workers before replying, while never autonomously waking or steering the agent during a user's reading/composition flow.
memory_remember confirmations and TUI rendering must omit stored memory IDs while retaining canonical content and any internal ID metadata needed by code.

Non-interrupting worker delivery will use a durable completion inbox and explicit subagent_wait tool; completions never trigger/steer the parent, waited records are consumed, and unconsumed records queue only at parent settlement for the next turn.

Proactive main-agent guidance must explicitly define the main agent as primary orchestrator responsible for user intent, worker coordination/waiting/synthesis, integration, and acceptance, while workers execute bounded delegated work.

Codex weekly quota footer colors use target clamp(14 × days until reset, 0, 100): green at/above target, yellow at/above half target, red below half, with fixed 20%/50% bands for absent, invalid, or expired resets.
Main-TUI spinner frames/settings are owned by the direct-root main-working-spinner extension, while Subagents directly owns and resets its wait-specific working message.

Main working-indicator configuration will ship fourteen named presets with a scoped preset enum and separate positive millisecond interval; animated presets default to 100 ms and Static ignores the interval.
Main working feedback is split: main-working-spinner owns only configurable indicator frames, while Subagents sets and clears its wait message directly without a shared wait-state event.
